transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (RiverMark CISO), Mark Evans (Dir Infra), Priya Kumar (Compliance), Alex Rivera (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync on POC security items: SSO integration, audit logs/export, data retention model during pilot, SOC2 evidence request, and a short discussion of encryption/KMS and RBAC mapping. Agreed on deliverables and next steps (see action items).

Topics:
- SSO / SAML mapping and group sync
- Audit log streaming and retention
- Data residency & retention policy during pilot
- SOC2 artifacts and pen-test report
- RBAC / admin controls and KMS key handling

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hi everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - we have Laura, Mark, Priya, Alex from RiverMark, and Daniel and I from Redwood.
[00:12] Laura Chen: Yep, thanks Sofia. We're on. Appreciate the quick follow up from last week, we've got a few blockers on SSO and the log pipeline.
[00:18] Daniel Cho: Cool, I'll start with SSO. Last week's SAML test hit a mapping issue where we weren't receiving the groups claim, so role mapping didn't populate. We pushed a small fix - however the staging IdP's assertion nameid is in email format and our mapping expected uid.
[00:35] Mark Evans: Right, that was the behavior. Our IdP is forcing email as NameID by default. Can Redwood accept that for group linking?
[00:43] Daniel Cho: Yes we can - we already have a mapping that can use email instead of uid, we just need to tweak the attribute mapping. I'm going to validate the attribute names; in some transcriptions it shows as name id or "name eye D"... sorry transcription issue.
[00:56] Laura Chen: Also want to confirm that group sync will map to RBAC roles and that admin role can't be granted automatically.
[01:03] Sofia Martinez: Correct. By default we require explicit admin assignment; group-to-role mapping can be controlled by your admins in the console or via SCIM. We can also disable automatic admin elevation.
[01:14] Priya Kumar: Can you remind us if Redwood supports SCIM for provisioning? We want to automate user lifecycle for the pilot.
[01:21] Daniel Cho: Yes, SCIM is supported. For the POC we recommended SAML + SCIM to keep user sync clean. SCIM provisioning will create users and populate group attributes so role mapping follows.
[01:33] Alex Rivera: When a user is deprovisioned from our IdP will the tokens/keys be revoked immediately?
[01:38] Daniel Cho: Session tokens are short lived; we also have a force revoke API that your ops can call. For highest safety we can reduce token TTL for the pilot.
[01:47] Mark Evans: Good. Onto audit logs - we tried to configure the S3 export last week and saw some missing fields in the sample events.
[01:54] Sofia Martinez: Sorry about that, we pushed a schema change and the sample format changed slightly; some fields moved under event.metadata. We'll send an updated sample and mapping doc.
[02:03] Laura Chen: The critical ask is that logs contain requestor identity, model id, route id, timestamps, and redaction markers for user PII. We need to forward to our SIEM.
[02:12] Daniel Cho: Understood. Our export contains user.email, request_id, model_name, route, timestamp, and an indicator if input was redacted. For PII we can mark events with redaction=true. We can also pseudonymize before export if required.
[02:25] Priya Kumar: About retention: currently RiverMark wants 90 days for pilot audit logs, but legal is pushing for 180 for certain regulated flows. Can Redwood hold 180?
[02:35] Sofia Martinez: Hosted default is 90 days for audit logs, but we can accommodate 180 on Dedicated or Private deployments. For the pilot on hosted we can retain 90 and provide on-demand export of older logs to your S3.
[02:47] Laura Chen: That export needs to be automated; we can't be manually pulling every week.
[02:51] Sofia Martinez: We'll set up automated export to your S3 with lifecycle rules. Daniel, can you confirm export cadence?
[02:56] Daniel Cho: We can do daily or hourly exports; daily is typical. We'll include a sample CloudTrail-style JSON with the fields Laura listed.
[03:06] Alex Rivera: Do you support server-side encryption with our customer-managed KMS for exported logs?
[03:11] Daniel Cho: For S3 exports we can sign objects with SSE-KMS using either Redwood-managed keys or you can provide a customer-managed key if using a Dedicated/Private deployment. For hosted we can set up SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS with Redwood keys; customer-managed KMS in hosted mode is limited due to multi-tenant constraints.
[03:29] Priya Kumar: That's an important point - if we require customer KMS for audit logs, that likely pushes us to Dedicated. Is there a cost delta we should expect?
[03:37] Sofia Martinez: Yes Dedicated has a pricing delta for reserved capacity. We'll include the approximate uplift in the pricing sheet we'll send after this call. For pilot purposes you can keep hosted and export to your KMS-enabled S3 bucket with server-side encryption - though key custody will be with Redwood-managed key unless you choose Dedicated.
[03:53] Mark Evans: On SOC2, Priya asked last week for the Type II report - did you get that?
[03:58] Sofia Martinez: We're SOC 2 Type II compliant. I'll send the latest report and the pen test summary. Note: some details in the pen-test are redacted for public distribution, but we can arrange an NDA if RiverMark needs full artifacts.
[04:12] Priya Kumar: We'll likely need the full pen-test under NDA. Also need the list of subprocessors and the data residency commitments.
[04:20] Sofia Martinez: We'll include the subprocessor list in the docs pack. For data residency: Redwood has regions in US and EU; for pilot we can pin to US region and ensure logs and data are stored in US.
[04:30] Laura Chen: During the pilot are prompts/input ever used for training? We cannot have our data used to train open models.
[04:36] Daniel Cho: By default Redwood does not use customer prompts for model training unless explicitly opted in. For enterprise accounts we have an explicit data use flag; by default in pilot it's disabled. We'll add that to the confirmation doc.
[04:47] Alex Rivera: What about model rollbacks and fallback behavior - if our dedicated model becomes unavailable, what's the fallback and are there cross-tenant data exposures?
[04:55] Daniel Cho: Fallbacks route to compatible model variants within same tenancy and do not intermix customer data. We have strict tenant isolation and runtime separation. For private deployments you get network-level isolation as well.
[05:07] Mark Evans: We heard from another vendor, PineAI, that they keep logs for longer but don't provide easy role mapping; seems like a tradeoff.
[05:13] Sofia Martinez: Yes each vendor has different defaults - we try to be explicit about retention and role mapping.
[05:18] Priya Kumar: A few small clarifying Qs: 1) Are there audit logs for admin actions in the console? 2) Is there an immutable log or append-only export? 3) Can we get alerts for suspicious admin behavior?
[05:27] Daniel Cho: 1) Yes, console admin actions are logged with actor and timestamp. 2) We offer append-only exports to your S3 bucket; you can enable object lock if you need WORM. 3) We can surface admin anomalies to your SIEM via exported events and we have role-based alerts; we can also set up webhook alerts for critical admin actions.
[05:44] Laura Chen: Great. On the SSO mapping test, we've seen intermittent failures where the group claim arrives but is named groupsList in your payload, not groups. Is that something you can tolerate?
[05:55] Daniel Cho: We can map arbitrary attribute names - we'll just need the exact attribute name (groupsList) and we'll wire it. For the SCIM mapping, ensure the group externalId is present.
[06:06] Sofia Martinez: Let's capture immediate next steps. We'll send SOC2 + pen test (NDA if required), updated log sample, and SAML/SCIM mapping guide. Daniel will run the SAML validation and test group mapping with your staging IdP.
[06:18] Priya Kumar: Can you also include a short note on data retention for embeddings and cached prefixes? We need to know if prompt caching persists beyond session.
[06:27] Daniel Cho: Prefix/KV cache is tenant-scoped and is configurable. For pilot we can disable persistent KV caching or set TTLs. Embeddings are stored for vector search features and retention is configurable; for RiverMark we can set a 90-day TTL or opt-out during the pilot.
[06:41] Mark Evans: Anything else on compliance?
[06:44] Laura Chen: No, that's it. If we get the SOC2 and pen test under NDA plus evidence of automated log export to S3 with SSE-KMS and object lock options, legal is comfortable to proceed to the next procurement step.
[06:58] Sofia Martinez: Perfect. We'll get those docs in the next 48 hours.
[07:02] Alex Rivera: One more ops question - for the audit log schema, can you add a request_latency_ms field? Our alerting rules need that.
[07:09] Daniel Cho: Sure, we'll include request_latency_ms and token_count fields.
[07:14] Priya Kumar: Thanks - also include a short blurb clarifying that Redwood does not use customer prompts to train models (we need that in writing).
[07:22] Sofia Martinez: Will do.
[07:24] Sofia Martinez: Ok recap of action items and owners - Daniel will validate SAML/SCIM mapping and run an end-to-end test (due 2026-05-25), I'll send SOC2 and pen test (NDA option) and subprocessor list (due 2026-05-22), Alex to provide S3 export details and CloudTrail field list (due: 2026-05-23), Priya to confirm retention targets (due 2026-05-24).
[07:43] Laura Chen: Sounds good. We'll review the docs and confirm next procurement steps after legal reviews the pen test.
[07:49] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we can reconvene next Tuesday same time if that works.
[07:54] Mark Evans: Works for me.
[07:56] Meeting ended.

References shared during call:
